assumptions.choice: A daily inverse Head and Shoulders is defined as five most-recent confirmed daily pivots ordered low-high-low-high-low, with the head lower than both shoulders. A pivot is confirmed when its high or low is respectively above or below the highs or lows of the adjacent daily bars.
assumptions.reason: The specification requires visual candle-based identification but provides no numerical pattern-recognition definition.

assumptions.choice: The neckline is the straight line through the two intervening high pivots; completion requires the daily close to cross from at-or-below the neckline to above it.
assumptions.reason: The specification states that price breaks the neckline upward but does not define the neckline geometry or breakout price field.

assumptions.choice: Weekly bars are constructed from the supplied daily feed. RSI uses Wilder's 14-period calculation on weekly closes. Positive divergence is identified from the two latest confirmed weekly low pivots: the latest low is lower and its RSI is higher.
assumptions.reason: The harness supplies only a daily feed, and the specification does not define weekly swing-low recognition.

assumptions.choice: The higher-timeframe trend is bullish when the latest completed monthly close is above the preceding completed monthly close.
assumptions.reason: The specification requires a bullish monthly trend but does not define its measurement.

assumptions.choice: Position size is the largest whole-share amount whose entry-price-to-stop loss is at most 1% of current broker equity, capped by available cash including commission.
assumptions.reason: The allowed loss range is 1-2%; 1% is selected as a concrete value within that stated range.

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss and take-profit triggers are checked against each daily bar's low and high and submit self.close(); if both are reached in one bar, the stop-loss has precedence.
assumptions.reason: The canonical convention defines exits as self.close(), while daily OHLC data cannot determine intrabar trigger order.
